svg.aria-label: Schematic convergent wedge: a backstop on the left pushes a wedge of sedimentary rock over a weak decollement; forethrusts and a backthrust cut the wedge, the surface slopes at alpha and the decollement dips at beta toward the backstop; below, a narrow steep wedge over a strong decollement beside a wide low wedge over salt
svg.text: Anatomy of a convergent wedge (schematic, vertically exaggerated)
DECOLLEMENT: weak layer (shale with high pore pressure, or salt)
Critical taper α + β: set by the strength of the wedge against the friction on the decollement
e.g. Taiwan, α + β ≈ 9°; mostly forethrusts
e.g. Zagros (Fars), α + β ≈ 1°; folds of both vergences
